# How to avoid explicitly constructing the 6×nv×nv frame Hessian during linearization of J(q+dq)^T λ in contact QP?

> **Current answer:** Confirm the target is the nv×nv matrix obtained from the space wrench λ contraction, not the full dJ/dq. The original thread indicates that the external-force term in RNEA includes J^Tλ, so the derivative d(J^Tλ)/dq can be directly calculated using RNEA analytical derivatives. The original author of Valkyrie nv=32 confirmed this method and reported that the derivative call is approximately 0.035 ms; these times are only representative of the old environment and should not be extrapolated.

## Key terms

- Recursive Newton-Euler Algorithm derivatives (RNEA derivatives) (递归牛顿-欧拉算法导数)
- External force (外部力)
- Tensor contraction (张量收缩)
- Finite difference (有限差分)

## Problem and symptoms

- How to avoid explicitly constructing the 6×nv×nv full kinematic Hessian during linearization of the contact QP using J(q+dq)^T λ?
- The full Hessian from finite difference impedes about 1 ms of computational budget; the actual target is to contract the first dimension of the Hessian and the contact wrench λ to obtain an nv×nv matrix.

## Environment

- 2019 Pinocchio/RBDL comparison; Valkyrie humanoid, nv=32; author only mentioned standard laptop, no CPU or precise Pinocchio version provided.

## Priority diagnostics

- First, write the real expression as J(q+dq)^T λ and confirm that the target is d(J^T λ)/dq, not the full dJ/dq.
- Distinguish between the Hessian-vector product of the tensor's last dimension and the nv×nv result from the original post along the space wrench dimension.

## Possible causes

- Explicit construction of the full Hessian would calculate unnecessary elements for the optimizer; RNEA external force term already includes J^T λ, so its analytical derivative can directly provide the required contraction.

## Attempts

- The author first used RBDL finite difference and discussed the full tensor API and nv time-variation calls.
- Subsequently, the RNEA derivatives for zero gravity, zero velocity/acceleration, and external force terms were used for dJ^T/dq·λ.

## Effective fixes

- If the target is indeed d(J^T λ)/dq, use the RNEA analytical derivatives with external forces directly, rather than first constructing the full frame Hessian.

## Result

- The author explicitly confirmed that RNEA derivatives can obtain the required Hessian-wrench product and reported the native Valkyrie comparison time sequence.

## Limitations

- 0.500/0.060/0.035 ms is a single author, old version, and unspecified CPU thread record; cannot be used as a current hardware benchmark.
- Maintainer estimates a standard laptop could reach 0.015 ms, but the author did not verify this value, and it is not included as a result here.
- If optimization truly requires the full dJ/dq, use the Pinocchio 4 frame kinematic Hessian interface instead of this contraction.

## Safety notes

- Compare the analytical contraction with finite difference in random q and λ directions before incorporating it into real-time contact QP.
